tips.comment: A War Eagle had a pretty eye-catching start to handicapping on last start and certainly impressed enough to justify the favourite tag in retrospect. Will improve and prove better than this field.
Harswell Ruby won in April at Doncaster. Disappointing last time, but with excuses and plenty of support, it is worth another go at these big odds.

Commander Of Life has yet to win on turf. His only two wins came on the all-weather, but with two 2nd places on turf in his last two runs, he cannot be far off his first turf win despite creeping up a pound for each of his last two runs.

With two good runs at Goodwood, when a close-up 2nd and a 3rd here over course and distance, veteran Orbaan has been knocking on the door. He may have missed his chance with his handicap mark going up 2lb, but he is very much in form and can make his presence felt at a decent each-way price.

This is wide open, and a chance is taken with outsider Liberty Bird, who has won over the course and distance and would have needed his recent run at Catterick, where he was bang there till late on when fitness told. Off of a dropping mark, he should be bang there.
Switched stables and stepped up to 1m2f on the last three runs, having previously run over 7f and 1m. More suited to 1m2f and in the Class 4 grade. Also acts on Good to Firm.

Another one from this stable who has not shown much in the last 3 outings but has also now dropped to a more competitive mark. With the hot form this trainer is in at the moment, you would not dismiss its chances.
Looks pretty well treated on old form and does like it here. Shimmering Sands rates the pick in an interesting race. Never got going at York last time, but this is doable.
Mark remains unchanged after LTO effort when 4th of 6 at Leicester earlier this month. It helps that he's a C&D winner and can be a serious threat despite going up in class.

I think Princess Niyla's last run is best ignored as she was eased when her chance had gone in a twenty-runner race at York. She ran two thirds and a win prior to that, and the twice course and distance could be in with a place.

Just five career runs for the 3yo filly. Two runs this year, solid efforts in handicap company, losing by just a neck three weeks ago. Same 10f trip and fast ground for this handicap. Plenty of room for improvement and she's facing much lower-rated rivals now.

Didn't get the best setup for the race at Donny last time seen over this distance and was always playing catch-up. As a result, I think you can look to upgrade that and see this as very generous odds.
Not in good form, but does have course experience and is now running off the lowest career mark. Hoping the longer trip suits her better, but it's the current mark that presents an opening.
Dr Rio has had three improving runs since the break in April and is now below his last winning mark. I think the return to 1m4f, which he won at here last year, could suit.

Three tuft runs for the 4yo this year. Excuses last time out and better judged on his previous run, which came over this 12f C/D. He was a good 2nd of 11 that day - good RPR rating - the 1st and 3rd both seemed capable types. A repeat of that form would put him firmly in the mix in this weak looking handicap.
Last Chance Saloon for this one, who reverts back to turf for the first time in over a year. Tentative each way bet and could nick a place.
Not in the best of form, but tends to do well here. It is now helped with a dropped mark, and the last win was off a higher mark, so it has a chance if in the right mood.

Hope Queen is an expensive Night Of Thunder filly from the powerful Karl Burke yard. She should be too strong first time out for Lingfield 2nd Private Project, who tried to make all against the stands rail but had no answer in the final furlong for Paroda Diva. She may make the running again around the bend into the straight at Beverley, but it is a stiff finish to hold off the two newcomers, Hope Queen and Conjecture.
No comment made

Shay Farmer takes over riding duties on Solar Biricz, and his 8lb claim could prove very valuable in negating the 6lb penalty, which in effect leaves him 2lb lower. He was tenacious in winning that, and he ran a good third here three runs ago.

Sanbona led until late over 6f at Redcar three days ago but dropped to 3rd place. Now, he goes over the minimum five furlongs for the first time. Drawn against the far rail, he could go close off bottom weight with a mark of only 49.

I reckon that Fair Call has a better chance than form and odds suggest here for the Camacho yard. The apprentice is as good as any claiming the 5 here in this race and really has to be doing better off this mark. Did stumble towards the end, so we will never know if the improvement was coming or not at the end of this horse's last race.

Tanjen makes her handicap debut and should be suited by the drop back to 5f. Although this filly hasn't troubled the judge in her three runs to date, she has shown early pace but has been running too keen over 6f and then failing to see it out at the finish.

This D & C Kubler trained 4-year-old gelding has won two races over seven furlongs on good to firm and good ground. The latest was nine days ago at Salisbury when keeping on well in the closing stages to beat the R M Beckett trained Noel Fox by 1 1/4 lengths. So with R Kingscote back in the saddle, he can defy his penalty and follow up today.

Great Blasket did not get a clear run last time out in a C5 but still got the win in the final strides. Although up 5 lbs for that to a 78, he did win a C3 off an 80 last summer. So today's C4 off a 78 could be doable.
Three times a winner here, once over course and distance. Just did enough when winning over a mile here last time out and should not be inconvenienced by this drop in trip.

Revolutionise looks a strong each-way play for me. Comes here from a break of 111 days and has often run well in the past fresh. He is the outsider of the field, but for me, this race looks open for us to get our nose in front. Williams has a good record at Brighton, and it's the only horse he's sending out tomorrow. I forgot to mention he is a course and distance winner and has very good ratings. I wouldn't write this one off.

This 3-year-old filly ran her best race yet for trainer W J Haggas in her latest start over six furlongs on good ground at Windsor 31 days ago when beaten 1 1/2 lengths in second of the nine runners behind the Alice Haynes-trained Far Above The Law. With Tom Marquand onboard for the first time, she can break her duck today.
Very impressive family and not a cheap purchase, Correspondence should benefit from the debut run to improve again and win here.

Wild Clary had a similar start last year when pants on debut but followed up with two C4 seconds. I am thinking that he will be all the better for that C4 run last week on the return from a break. He has a very handy Alec Volikhansky in the saddle, claiming 3 lbs with a drop to C5, so is in with a chance for me.
Connections are clearly trying to take full advantage of BANKSMAN's hot streak. With not too many rivals to worry about, he's taken to land the hat trick.
River Wharfe looked to be delivering a winning challenge last time out at Brighton despite the rise in the weights and can imagine that being the case again here. Value bet at the odds.
Sol Argent won here in May off a 55 but could not follow up after taking on 5 lbs. However, it could bounce back with the return here and a 59 today.

Throne Hall has won 5 races from 1 mile to 2 miles and also won 3 over hurdles. His latest outing at Haydock saw him finish 4th over 1 mile 4 furlongs. This season has seen Throne Hall win at Les Landes and Musselburgh.

A very consistent mare who has won 3 from 10 over today's course and distance. With a 5lb claim, she runs here off a mark lower than the last time she won, which was here off 46 in April 2024. The John Berry mare receives weight from all 5 rivals and can make that tell.
Makes stable debut for John Gallagher and could benefit from the drop in trip after racing over a mile here earlier this month.
Mr. Ubiquitous won last time out by over 2L and goes again off the same mark and the same rider, who is now claiming 7 lbs. So, barring any mistakes, he could be bang in there again.

Graduated looks a bit overpriced for me in this. That's all there is to it really. Mr Ubiquitous is well treated, but with an inexperienced jockey on top, he may bolt off a bit too quick, so I'm not keen at the price. Graduated looks like a good play.
This Farh benefited from the application of cheekpieces when going in by over two lengths after leading all the way last time out.

Tolerance, for me, is the one to beat tomorrow regardless of how the market is looking. First time cheekpieces and back down in trip 7f with Buick riding. Still a maiden, but it's a risk I'm willing to take.

Miss Honey made an eye-catching winning debut over this distance at Kempton 13 days ago. Sluggishly away, green, it wasn't until near the line she was hitting top gear. Under a hands and heels ride from W. Buick, she won going away. That is the stand-out form on offer. She will come on a bundle for that initial experience. Her pedigree suggests the switch to turf shouldn't be a problem. If anything, it should suit the selection. The Godolphin filly is turned out quickly under a penalty by J. Gosden, who wouldn't really be one to rush one. He must feel she is ready to push on. The trainer won this in 2022. Godolphin also won this in 2019 and 2021. Favourites have a strong record in this particular contest, winning 4 of the last 5 runnings. There are a few fairly interesting debutants in here who will need a market check, but it will take an above-average one, however, to beat this filly.
Mystic Moment has two creditable runs under the belt and this could be what the horse is crying out for, having raced over shorter trips. Great chance.

This could turn out to be a decent novice race, and Speculative will be just that, a speculative each way on her debut. She cost £72K as a yearling, was an early foal, and her dam was a 7f winner and placed at Listed level. Trainer Tom Dascombe has a fair record with debutants and a profitable record with his juvenile fillies on debut.

Stardinia slightly disappointed in her second outing to be only 5th at Ascot after being 2nd first time out at Leicester. But both runs were against decent opponents, and she has every chance of her first win moving up to 6f at Newbury.
Sinj has been knocking on the door recently with 2 runner-ups in its 2 races. At 9/2, it is worth a small wager.

Due Destiny was unlucky at the start of the month on debut at 6f with a duff start that put her on the back foot. She did not fare so well last time out at 5f and was up against the boys. But I think the return to 6f and running with the fillies, and Laura on top claiming 3 lbs, could be worth an EW chance.

Hydroplane was running for the first time in over two years when a decent 3rd of 12 in a handicap at Chester off a mark of 78. The nine-year-old may be long in the tooth, and his last win was at Chester in June 2022 off 76, but he may still be up to another win.
Almuhit had three cracking runs over hurdles this spring and showed encouragement with a good fourth in a class 3 at Goodwood two weeks ago.
Just 3 wins from 21 runs. Not great, but only 3 lbs higher than the last winning mark, and it helps that she has experience. C&D winner and conditions should favor her.

All Bashful Boy's best form looks to be at galloping tracks, so the first two runs of this year can be discounted if my analysis is correct. Bashful Boy is 9 years old but is still capable down in class, on a low mark, and Jack Dace is taking another 7 lbs off. All the money is for the Balding/Buick combo, but their entry has disappointed and will be over-backed.

Two turf runs for the 4yo filly this year. Beaten just a hd two starts back and she followed that with an impressive 1L+ win three weeks ago, heavily eased down in the last half furlong. I like the fact that the next four home all came into the race in good form. Same jockey on board for this apprentice handicap, higher mark but she can follow up.

The jockey has piloted Ocean Heights to win 2 from 3, which surely must count for a lot in an apprentice handicap. The gelding was fourth off 81 over a slightly longer trip at this track in August last year and gets in this lower class contest off 69 today. Dace will probably try to make all today and should be difficult to pass.

Boy George is an old favorite of mine and has returned from a break in May to win the first two runs, with the latest being by 1L. He has only risen 2 lbs and could swing a hat-trick like at the start of last term.

Mojomaker has only won once, and that was as a two-year-old. Now, as a six-year-old, he is running consistently well and is overdue for a second win. He has been 3rd in four of his six races this year, and Rossa Ryan is booked to ride again. He looked unlucky with his draw last time at Chepstow, as he was stuck out wide throughout when two lengths 5th of 10, losing two places late on. He has been dropped another pound to his lowest ever mark of 69.

Trainer Christopher Mason and jockey Gina Mangan are flying at the moment and have had 3 winners and a second from their last 4 runners. On Edge represents them at Newbury this evening. He is their only runner of the meeting and ran a nice race first time out this season. He is on the same mark as his last win, so looks to have a good chance here.

The 10yo has been good for connections, win or placed in 36 races. He probably needed his three runs this year to get his fitness up to scratch, and was a good 3rd of 10 two weeks ago, only beaten a length after staying on from the rear. He was rated a huge 20lb higher this time last year.

The 4yo has been ridden by apprentice riders in his three runs this year, three near misses and good RPR ratings. The form of his previous race looks solid. Runner-up last time out and 5L clear of the rest. Good jockey Rossa Ryan now takes over in the saddle and he can get a little bit extra out of the selection.
No comment made
The horse was in a tough race last time out. This race is more to the horse's liking. Looks like a nice each-way chance with the trip and ground suitable.
Kept on inside the final furlong over a mile in a Class 4 on soft ground at Goodwood earlier this month. The ease in grade to Class 5, drop in trip to 7 furlongs and the quicker ground appeal.

A very open but competitive handicap in which Byzantine Empress could go close. This ex-Irish filly has only one win to her name but has been placed many times. Conditions look ideal, and if she improves for the first-time cheekpieces, she could notch another success.

Time To Bite last saw a hurdle over three years ago. He developed into a decent front-running chaser and won three of his last five chases. His hurdle form in Ireland was nothing special, often going clear early and fading well before the finish. But it could be that he has improved with age. Now a ten-year-old and less headstrong, he could go close to making most over two miles five and a half furlongs around the sharp Newton Abbot hurdles track.

The model I run suggests Kill The Groove can win this one. This result has been driven by Kill The Groove having the second highest RPR of the 8 runners here, but an official ranking that is the second lowest. This subsequently means Kill The Groove goes out with the joint lowest amount of weight to carry around this 2m 5f round trip. Has placed with two third place finishes recently and needs to improve to get over the line first. Model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which has been driven by a combination of the small gap back to second in the race simulation but reasonable value on offer here at 6.5s. This translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
This has just got a really obvious chance after finishing second over C&D last time out. I think a repeat will see it win.

The model I run suggests Stiletto can win this one. Stiletto lines up here with the highest RPR by quite an amount and has an official ranking leaving this horse very well treated off this mark. Sean Bowen champion jockey picks up the reins and is trusted pair of hands. Stiletto last ran 20 days ago so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Prairie Queen was second in March and was doing a good job until falling two out. Worth another shot as she is now second up after wind surgery, which is when I would expect more.
Limerick Leader was a close second here at the start of this month after a short break in a C4. The drop to C5 while up just 1 lb for that last run could be enough to get back on the top step.

Romanor, an 11-year-old who has been falling down the handicap, has shown positive signs of returning to form in his last two starts. He has a very good record here, including three wins. The ground and trip are ideal, and his last run was in a class 4, so on paper, this is easier. Expect to see him come through with a late surge, and the price offers some value if he times it right.

Slievegar looked back to form when he was run out of it on the run-in last time after a mistake at the last fence when 2nd of 4 at Warwick over three miles one and a half furlongs. The drop in distance may help this time at Newton Abbot.

Was always going to be a handicapper for Paul Nichols and Old Gold Racing and has been given 4 maiden runs to get plenty of experience into the horse. First run in a handicap over what looks like a good trip. Race doesn't look too tough and a good run is expected by the stable.

Clearance is now an eleven-year-old but still capable of winning hurdle races. He has seen a falling mark since winning consecutive hurdle races here in May and June 2024 off marks of 108 and 112. He is now dropped to only 103, and although joint top weight here, he should go close.

Colonel Lesley had a comeback run here about 3 weeks ago and performed creditably even though only 6th. He will have needed that run, and with the pace he has in this sort of grade, he should be able to be there or thereabouts. The jockey is competent.

FEEL THE PINCH is a stone lower than his C&D victory here in July last year. This may have been plotted having been run frequently in the winter months. Good jockey booking and I'm hopeful of a big run.

Manyana Blue is a frontrunner on the flat who is still a maiden, weakening late on over both a mile and ten furlongs. She has a similar mark on the flat to the favorite Blue Tempus, who is also a maiden and did not do any better for moving up in distance from ten furlongs to twelve furlongs last time at Doncaster, finishing last of seven. The better value is with Manyana Blue as Newton Abbot is a sharp track that favors frontrunners.

The model I run suggests Return With Gold can win this data-light juvenile maiden hurdle. Experience tends to be important over these kinds of events, and Return With Gold is the only one who has form figures to go by. The only prior race was a healthy 3rd place finish and should come on from that. All horses, bar one or two, go out carrying the same amount of weight, and Return With Gold last ran out 17 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Radharc Na Slaine can win this one. This result has been driven by Radharc Na Slaine having a comparably high RPR to the other 7 runners, but goes out carrying the second lowest amount of weight thanks to an attractive-looking mark. Radharc Na Slaine has some reliable placed efforts over the recent form figures but needs improvement to go one better here. Last ran 20 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be an issue, and over a stone less than the current top weight and market leader over this 3m 1f trip should be telling by the end. The model has issued a 'low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Testflight is down to a basement mark of 67, his lowest ever. But at age eight, he should be near his peak as a chaser. He has been pointing this year, gaining his first-ever win in a maiden conditions point last month at Cothelstone, jumping much better than he finished off the previous year under rules. He could now be capable of exploiting his very low mark back under rules with Tabitha Worsley taking his weight below ten stone.

Janeslittlevoice has plenty of stamina, has won over CD (heavy), and has won on good at Wincanton 3m. The lightly raced 11yo pulled up on return after a 518-day layoff before finishing 2nd here. The next two starts at Fontwell can be forgiven; hampered and lost a shoe on the penultimate run and was out of the handicap last time. Those runs would have kept her in good shape for her return here, and the rider can make use of her 7lb claim.

Remains unexposed in handicaps and should be very competitive in this grade, especially considering the 4th on penultimate start at Doncaster behind Blue Hop, who has won again since. That race was far more competitive. Should build on the comeback 2nd LTO.

This was smashed up into favourite at the last meeting here, but they had quite a bit of rain and he was pulled out. I'm not really sure what trip he wants exactly, but the latest third after a wind op was certainly more encouraging and this race looks winnable.

Gateau Miel won over fences at Stratford last week, ridden by Tom Broughton, and now reverts to hurdles off the same mark. He last ran over hurdles in November 2021 when Rachael Blackmore rode him to be 4th of 21 in a three-mile handicap hurdle at Punchestown off 106. He had been pointing earlier this year and then ran a close 2nd of 6 in a hunter chase over a similar distance. Could be up to following up back over hurdles.

Danzini runs this course well, having 4 placed finishes from 5 starts. The 9-year-old has shown all its best form on good ground and at this trip. The yard has come straight here for the seasonal opener, which suggests she's ready to go. Was only beaten a length over CD in August 2023 when returning from a break. Good enough to win - but is she fully fit? With the yard in good form, a good strike rate here and today's chosen rider are reasons enough to believe so, and the price of 11/1 offers some value he's ready.

Presenting Yeats could be worth an EW shot as he won on the return in April by nearly 10L. He took on 8 lbs for that but has now dropped to just 2 lbs above that last winning mark, which puts him well light among today's C4 runners.
